title: P0 KV prefetch throttle - streaming tail latency & 5xx cascade
summary: On 2027-03-10 at 15:12 UTC Redwood Hosted API experienced a P0 incident: elevated tail latency for streaming responses and a cascade of 5xx errors lasting ~18 minutes. Root cause was an over-aggressive KV prefetch throttle combined with a scheduler bug that cancelled in-flight prefetches for long-lived streaming sessions. Result: increased KV cache misses, blocked token generation, and client-visible 5xx/timeouts for streaming sessions. Impacted ~14% of production requests; top-tier customers saw degraded streaming quality and reconnects.
impact: Duration: 15:12–15:30 UTC (approx 18 minutes) with residual mitigation until 15:45. Affected surface: hosted API streaming endpoints (server-sent events and websocket streaming). Severity: P0. Customer impact: increased client disconnects, repeated 502/504 errors and delays; estimated 14% of requests with streaming enabled experienced >=2x latency and 5xx. No data loss; some user sessions retried and regained service after reconnect.
timeline:
15:06 UTC - Pre-incident: rollout of prefetch budget reduction (256->64) began (canary)
15:11 UTC - Canary metric anomalies start: prefetch queue latency rising in canary region
15:12 UTC - Production alert: streaming tail latency SLO breach + 5xx spike threshold crossed; oncall paged
15:13 UTC - SREs confirm correlated spike in kv-prefetch queue time and prefetch cancellations
15:16 UTC - First mitigation: increase prefetch budget to 128 for affected region; partial improvement observed
15:20 UTC - Root cause hypothesis validated: scheduler bug cancelling prefetches for half-closed streaming sessions; emergency rollback of throttle config initiated
15:23 UTC - Full rollback to previous prefetch budget (256) completed across regions; error rate declines
15:30 UTC - 5xx and latency return to baseline
15:45 UTC - Post-incident monitoring shows stability; incident declared resolved
detection: Triggered by streaming-tail-latency SLO dashboard alerts (Grafana) and a surge in 5xx rate alarms. Oncall first noticed increased prefetch queue latencies and concurrent prefetch cancellation logs (prefetch_cancelled=true) in the infra logs. PagerDuty runbook pointed to kv-prefetch as high-likelihood area.
root_causes:
1) Configuration change: a canary rollout reduced global per-node prefetch budget from 256 to 64 to lower memory pressure. The config change was rolled forward despite higher-than-expected prefetch queueing in canary.
2) Scheduler bug: when sessions entered half-closed or paused states (common with client-initiated pauses in streaming), the prefetch scheduler cancelled in-flight prefetch jobs without rescheduling, producing sudden cache misses.
3) Throttle algorithm uses absolute node-level throughput rather than per-session allocation, allowing storms from many small sessions to exhaust the budget and trigger aggressive cancellation.
contributing_factors:
1) Insufficient canary guardrails — canary alert thresholds were not sensitive to queue latency metrics.
2) Lack of sentinel metrics for prefetch cancellation rate; cancellations appeared only in debug logs.
3) No automated rollback trigger tied to sustained prefetch queue growth or cancellation rate.
4) Documentation gaps: runbook did not include the 'half-closed' scheduler failure mode.
mitigations:
Immediate: rolled back prefetch budget to 256; temporarily disabled the new cancellation path in scheduler; increased prefetch queue capacity and extended prefetch worker timeouts.
Short-term: deployed a hotfix to prevent cancellations for streaming sessions and instrumented cancellation counters as surfaced metrics.
Long-term: plan to redesign throttle to be per-session-aware and add automatic rollback triggers and runbook checks.
action_items:
A1: Patch scheduler to not cancel in-flight prefetches for streaming sessions (owner: Marco) - ETA 2027-03-17
A2: Rework prefetch throttle algorithm to include per-session allocation and fairness (owner: Evelyn) - ETA 2027-04-05
A3: Add cancellation_rate, queue_latency_95/99, queue_growth alerts to Grafana and tie to automated canary rollback (owner: Samir) - ETA 2027-03-24
A4: Update hosted-api runbook: steps to detect prefetch storms and immediate rollback instructions (owner: Priya) - ETA 2027-03-16
A5: Postmortem review with product teams to assess rollout criteria for memory-related throttles (owner: Jared) - ETA 2027-03-22
runbook_updates: 1) New section: 'KV prefetch storm' with checklist: check prefetch_budget, queue_latency percentiles, cancellation_rate metric, recent config rollouts. 2) Add explicit rollback commands and verification queries. 3) Add runbook test in staging that simulates many paused streaming sessions.
communication: Customer communications: drafted status note for status.redwood.ai and emailed affected customers via account execs. Internal comms: incident channel #p0-kv-prefetch and a postmortem review meeting scheduled. PR to add incident summary to weekly SRE digest.
lessons_learned:
1) Small config changes affecting resource budgets can have outsized effects on streaming workloads with bursty per-session behavior.
2) Metric coverage matters: important failure modes (prefetch cancellations) were buried in logs rather than surfaced as metrics.
3) Canary rollouts must include queueing metrics and automated rollback thresholds for memory/throughput-related changes.
